Morgan: Hi all, first-week question I need kube access for dev+staging and a namespace `redwood-morgan`. Also want to port-forward a pod and avoid accidentally adding prod to my kubeconfig. Whats the quick recommended process?

Jamie (DevEx): Welcome! :tada: Our flow is: 1) submit the access form for namespace + kubeconfig, include manager and duration; 2) SRE approves and we mint a short-lived kubeconfig scoped to requested clusters only; 3) use the provided merge script to add it to your local config without touching prod contexts.

Jamie (DevEx): Link to form: https://redwood.internal/access-requests (choose "Kubernetes namespace + kubeconfig"). Typical default duration for new hires is 30 days.

Priya (eng-infra): To add detail: we create a serviceaccount in the namespace and issue a kubeconfig that references a short-lived token exchange (no long-lived SA tokens in your dotfiles). That kubeconfig contains only dev and staging contexts. Prod is explicitly excluded unless you request it via separate SSO + manager approval.

Carlos (SRE): For port-forwarding we grant pods/portforward in the namespace Role. If you need `kubectl proxy` that's fine for most UI debugging. Node-level access or hostNetwork requires escalated approvals.

Morgan: If my manager is OOO, who approves? Also, can I run local `kubectl proxy` with the issued kubeconfig to hit our local UI?

Jamie (DevEx): If manager is OOO, add the team lead in the "alternate approver" field on the form; SRE will hit the on-call manager alias as fallback. And yes, `kubectl proxy --kubeconfig=./morgan-kc.yaml` is allowed for dev/staging.

Priya (eng-infra): After you get morgan-kc.yaml, this is our recommended merge snippet to avoid mixing contexts:

```bash
# merge without clobbering prod
export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:./morgan-kc.yaml
kubectl config view --merge --flatten > /tmp/merged && mv /tmp/merged ~/.kube/config
# switch to the namespace-scoped context
kubectl config use-context redwood-dev/morgan
```

Priya (eng-infra): Security tip: do NOT copy tokens into dotfiles. Keep the provided file in your home or use the helper that adds it to your credential cache.

access-bot: Access request created: AR-4827  Namespace redwood-morgan, clusters: dev, staging, duration: 30d. Assigned to SRE. Link: https://redwood.internal/requests/AR-4827

Carlos (SRE): I reviewed and marked approved with fallback. Created Role/RoleBinding for `pods/portforward` in namespace and bound a serviceaccount. Kubeconfig is attached to the ticket, tokens rotate every 24h by default (we can extend for onboarding).

Morgan: I see the kubeconfig and merged it using the snippet. `kubectl get pods -n redwood-morgan` works and `kubectl port-forward` to my debug pod succeeded. Thanks everyone!

Jamie (DevEx): Great, add this to your onboarding checklist and ping us if anything times out or you hit auth errors. :+1:
